claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me. I wanted to check if I can still claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few questions.

Since Alex is 17, the key factor is whether he's in approved education or training. **Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs, or an approved training course)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's doing his Highers at college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex is 17 and in approved education (doing his Highers), that's good for eligibility purposes.

Now I need to ask: **Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Edinburgh.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. A few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Does Alex live with you, or if he doesn't live with you full-time, do you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards his upkeep?** (Child Benefit includes things like food, clothes, or pocket money)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just one more important question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (Remember, only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, no one else is claiming for him. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 17 and studying his Highers at college, which counts as approved education
- You can continue to receive Child Benefit for children under 20 who remain in approved education or training
- You live in the UK and Alex lives at home with you, so you're responsible for him
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

**Important things to remember:**
- You'll continue to be eligible as long as Alex stays in approved education or training and remains under 20
- If Alex's circumstances change (for example, if he leaves education, starts working 24+ hours per week, or starts claiming certain benefits in his own right), you must inform HMRC as this could affect your entitlement
- Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit tax charge if you or your partner earn over £60,000 individually

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. If you're already receiving it, you should continue to be eligible under these circumstances.
